items.fromString:
Currently, once an OpenSCAP policy is created, its name cannot be changed in either the UI or backend, which makes testing and iterative configuration difficult.

While running tests with different policies and rules, the customer often needs to adjust naming conventions. At present, this requires creating an entirely new policy, which is both unnecessary and time-consuming.

Additionally, creating a new policy results in a new policy ID. This forces updates in automation scripts that assign policies to newly provisioned hosts, adding extra manual effort and increasing the risk of errors.

Allowing policy names to be edited without changing the policy ID would significantly reduce operational overhead and improve efficiency during testing and policy management.

At present, Hybrid Cloud Console can be integrated with AWS , Azure, and GCP. And using the integration or using the information directly from the cloud accounts, Image Builder can create blueprints, connect to those clouds, and deploy images there. 

 

Now, A specical situation is there with MS Azure China, which is separate from MS Azure itself and has quite a lot of limitations. 

 

There are some end-user requirements to be able to build and push images via Hosted Image Builder to Azure China but they can't do as it's not configurable and supported yet. This RFE requests for that support.
items.toString:
*Overview*
Provide hosted RHEL image builder support for creating and sharing custom images with Microsoft Azure China accounts.

*Background*
The RHEL image builder service on the Hybrid Cloud Console supports creating custom images for Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. For AWS, Google, and Azure, users enter additional authentication information during blueprint creation so that the built custom images are shared with their cloud accounts. Similar authentication methods can be used in a blueprint when building a custom image with image-builder cli on a RHEL host to upload the image a cloud provider account.

Microsoft Azure China uses separate authentication from Microsoft Azure in other regions, and so requires an authentication schema and workflow that is not currently supported by RHEL image builder. The current solution for users to build custom RHEL images for Microsoft Azure China is:

* Write a blueprint for the custom image. Example for a vhd image type: [https://osbuild.org/docs/user-guide/image-descriptions/rhel-10.1/vhd/|https://osbuild.org/docs/user-guide/image-descriptions/rhel-10.1/vhd/|smart-link] 
* Build the vhd image on a RHEL host
* Manually upload the resulting image to Microsoft Azure China following this guide: [https://access.redhat.com/articles/uploading-rhel-image-to-azure|https://access.redhat.com/articles/uploading-rhel-image-to-azure|smart-link] 

An alternative workflow for users who want a guided blueprint experience is to build a virtualization (.qcow2) image with hosted RHEL image builder, download the image, configure and convert the image to .vhd format, and upload to Microsoft Azure China. This procedure is documented in this guide: [https://access.redhat.com/articles/uploading-rhel-image-to-azure#header23|https://access.redhat.com/articles/uploading-rhel-image-to-azure#header23|smart-link] 

*Outcomes / Use Cases*

* When creating a blueprint in the hosted RHEL image builder service, a customer can select 'Microsoft Azure China' as a target and enter the authentication information required to share images with their Microsoft Azure China account.
* When building an image from that blueprint, the resulting image is successfully shared to their Microsoft Azure China account.

Consider a scenario where two Satellite servers are connected to a single account, both syncing their inventories. A host named {{client1.example.com}} was originally registered with {{satellite1.example.com}} while running RHEL 8.7.

Later, this host was unregistered from {{{}satellite1.example.com{}}}, registered with {{{}satellite2.example.com{}}}, and upgraded to RHEL 8.10. However, the old host profile (RHEL 8.7) was not removed from {{{}satellite1.example.com{}}}.

As a result, when inventory data is synced from both Satellite servers, two entries for the same host are uploaded—each reflecting different OS versions, which is expected behavior. However, without visibility into which Satellite each record was sourced from, it's difficult to accurately identify and manage such discrepancies.



*Proposed Solution:*
Include the Satellite server name (e.g., {{satellite1.example.com}} or {{{}satellite2.example.com{}}}) in the Data Collector metadata for each host record. This enhancement will enable users to:
 * Clearly distinguish between records sourced from different Satellite servers.

 * Identify stale or outdated profiles.

 * Take appropriate action, such as removing old entries or reconciling data conflicts.

This small addition would significantly improve data clarity and operational efficiency when managing host inventory in multi-Satellite environments.

Modify the Inventory host view to include the name of the specific Satellite in the Data Collector.

At present, it only shows that synchronization is occurring with a Satellite, without identifying which Satellite is involved.

Suppose there are two satellite servers connected to one account, and both are syncing their inventory. 
There was one host with the name "client1.example.com" earlier when it was on RHEL8.7 was registered with satellite1.example.com, 

Later, client1.example.com got unregistered from satellite1.example.com and got registered with satellite2.example.com and upgraded client from RHEL8.7 to RHEL8.10, but the old profile, which has RHEL8.7 OS, was not deleted from satellite1.example.com

So in this scenario, when inventory is getting synced from both satellite servers, it uploads the same client's profile with the same name but with a different OS, which is expected.

If we provide the details of the satellite in the Data Collector by from which satellite it got synced, it will be helpful to identify and take the appropriate action accordingly.

Later, this host was unregistered from {{{}satellite1.example.com{}}}, registered with {{{}satellite2.example.com{}}}, and upgraded to RHEL 8.10. However, the old host profile (RHEL 8.7) was not removed from {{{}satellite1.example.com{}}}.

As a result, when inventory data is synced from both Satellite servers, two entries for the same host are uploaded—each reflecting different OS versions, which is expected behavior. However, without visibility into which Satellite each record was sourced from, it's difficult to accurately identify and manage such discrepancies.



*Proposed Solution:*
Include the Satellite server name (e.g., {{satellite1.example.com}} or {{{}satellite2.example.com{}}}) in the Data Collector metadata for each host record. This enhancement will enable users to:
 * Clearly distinguish between records sourced from different Satellite servers.

 * Identify stale or outdated profiles.

 * Take appropriate action, such as removing old entries or reconciling data conflicts.

This small addition would significantly improve data clarity and operational efficiency when managing host inventory in multi-Satellite environments.

h2. 1. Problem Statement

For customers operating OpenShift clusters in disconnected environments, the current process for uploading Insights Operator archives to Red Hat relies on command-line tools. The prescribed method involves using a {{curl}} command to post the {{tar.gz}} file to {{console.redhat.com/api/ingress/v1/upload [1].}}

This approach presents several challenges:
 * *Poor User Experience:* The command-line interface is not intuitive for all users, especially those who are not comfortable with or do not have easy access to a command line with the {{curl}} utility. This can lead to user frustration and errors during the upload process.

 * *Lack of Feedback:* The {{curl}} command provides minimal feedback on the status of the upload. Users do not get clear, visual confirmation that the file is being uploaded or that it has been successfully received and is being processed.

 * *Error Prone:* The manual nature of the {{curl}} command increases the likelihood of errors, such as typos in the command or incorrect file paths. Troubleshooting these issues can be time-consuming.

 * *Inconsistent with Web-based Management:* The rest of the {{console.redhat.com}} experience is web-based. Forcing users to drop to a command line for this specific task is inconsistent with the overall user experience of the platform.

h2. 2. Proposed Solution

This Request for Enhancement (RFE) proposes the creation of a dedicated web page on {{console.redhat.com}} that allows customers to upload their Insights Operator archives directly through their web browser.

This page should include the following features:
 * A clear and simple file upload interface (e.g., a "drag and drop" area and/or a "browse" button).

 * Visual feedback during the upload process, such as a progress bar.

 * Clear success or failure messages upon completion of the upload.

 * Links to relevant documentation about the Insights Operator and the archive upload process.

h2. 3. User Story

As a cluster administrator for a disconnected OpenShift environment, I need to upload our Insights Operator archive to Red Hat to work with RH Insights. Currently, I have to find the correct {{curl}} command and run it from a terminal. I would prefer to be able to log into {{{}console.redhat.com{}}}, navigate to a dedicated upload page, and upload the archive file directly from my browser. This would be a much more intuitive and user-friendly process, and it would give me more confidence that the upload was successful.
h2. 4. Benefits
 * *Improved User Experience:* A web-based upload page will provide a more intuitive and user-friendly experience for all customers, regardless of their comfort level with the command line.

 * *Reduced Errors:* A guided, web-based workflow will reduce the likelihood of user error during the upload process.

 * *Increased Adoption:* A simpler upload process may encourage more customers with disconnected clusters to utilize the RH Insights, leading to better support outcomes.

 * *Consistent Platform Experience:* This enhancement will align the Insights Operator archive upload process with the rest of the web-based {{console.redhat.com}} platform.

 

 [1] https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/support/remote-health-monitoring-with-connected-clusters#insights-operator-manual-upload_remote-health-reporting-from-restricted-network

items.fromString:
h4. Feature Overview

Currently when building images, the BaseOS and Appstream repos are used, and the user can select custom repositories to add, but additional red hat repositories cannot be used when building the image.  This feature would allow the user to optionally add additional Red Hat repositories
h4. Background and Strategic Fit

This would enable the Extensions repo in Image builder: [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHIN-1966]
h4. Goals
 * Build images with add on repositories such as Code Ready builder and the Extensions repo
 * Build images with add on products such as High Availablity

h4. Requirements
|*requirement*|*Notes*|*Is Mvp?*|
|User can add layered repositories that do not require an additional subscription| |Y|
|User can add layered repositories that do not require an additional subscription
 | |Y|
|User should only be able to add repositories they have a subscription for| |Y|
|Enable repositories after registration if registration is enabled|?| |

 
h4. Non-Functional Requirements

N/A
h4. Use Cases (User Experience & Workflow)
 # A user would go to Images to build an image
 # Use would create a blueprint
 # User would select RHEL 9
 # User would proceed through the wizard until they get to the "Repositories" step (Formally custom repositories)
 # User could select one or more additional Red Hat repositories in addition to the custom repositories
 # User would continue to the packages screen and add packages from these additional Red Hat repositories
 # User would continue and build the image
 # Built image would contain packages from these custom repositories

h4. Customer Considerations
 * Activation Keys - how much do we ensure repositories are enabled after the system boots and is registered.
 * Offer ability to 'clone' activation key and add new repositories
 * Enable repositories in first boot

h4. Customer Information/Supportability

 
h4. Documentation Considerations
 * Documentation updates around the "Custom repositories" wizard step, as well as how to add additional repositories

The RHEL AppStream Life Cycle is complex, and this is also reflected in the life cycle of first-party containers in the Ecosystem Catalog.  This means it is easy for a customer to deploy an official container image that soon becomes deprecated and no longer receives functional or security updates via `podman auto-update` (or similar).  This may silently lead to a running an insecure version of containerized software, even though packages on the host are up-to-date.

As a concrete example, the ubi8/nginx-120 container image was marked as "deprecated" in the ecosystem catalog in November 2023, when the underlying AppStream for Nginx 1.20 reached the end of life. ([https://catalog.redhat.com/software/containers/ubi8/nginx-120/6156abfac739c0a4123a86fd)]  No mechanism currently flags that local ubi8/nginx-120 are deprecated and no longer receiving updates; simply no updates appear in the upstream repository.

Ideally this would also flag on running containers that are FROM (layered upon) known-deprecated images, as client-local images often apply limited customization on top of upstream ubi/rhel images and would also be silently vulnerable.

This WIP presentation from Brian Smith discusses how pervasive this problem is, primarily in the context of Image Builder: [https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1RrVwNnkROR4GIcRkww1ArrAVfgCRzcxG-mpfW_O8_I8/edit|https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1RrVwNnkROR4GIcRkww1ArrAVfgCRzcxG-mpfW_O8_I8/edit#slide=id.p]  In the sample set, over 70% of (non-containerized) deployments of nginx and NodeJS on RHEL 8 are running from deprecated AppStreams.

items.fromString:
h2. Description of Problem

Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console Inventory does not display the field "Created By : Login ID/Activation Key"  after opening the system profile in the inventory.

Since the older inventory ([https://access.redhat.com/management/systems]) is now deprecated and migrated to the new inventory ([https://console.redhat.com/insights/inventory]), so customer wanted to know who has created the system profile in the inventory or which user has registered the system profile. Previously on the Red Hat Customer Portal they could see which username was used to register a system.

 

On Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console, although we can find the Registered date under System status section, there is no field which specifies the username/activation key who registered the system like Created By on Customer Portal.

Activation keys are used by many customers at a departmental level to allow registration of systems. Customers would like a means to show which activation keys(s) were used to register a system so that they could track usage at a per-departmental level. 

 

As a Org-Admin, customer would like to know details of the system profiles reported to the HBI and they would like to know which login ID/activation key was used by a user to register a system so that they can do housekeeping. In case of over utilization/registration, they can reach out to the respective user to limit the registrations.

 

For directly connected servers, we could use subscription-manager information to display which login ID/activation key was used.

 

For satellite connected servers where the data is reported via satellite inventory upload plugin, customer could match the system profile in satellite inventory to find the actual user ID/activation key for consumer profile but it is not possible for the directly connected servers as HBI is the only place where the details are visible.

For satellite connected servers, we could display the created by : satellite activation key.

 

Similar RFE but this is only for exposing the actual activation key details in the inventory [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/BIZ-639]

 

 

For the public cloud systems which are registered through auto-registration option, inventory should display the   "Created By : Cloud based Auto-registration"
h2.
items.toString:
h2. Description of Problem
For organizations that have many users registering systems, it can be difficult to know where the systems came from. Providing some level of information about how the system was registered would help Org Admins better sort and manage their inventory and provide them with a better path to identifying system ownership.

For example, activation keys are used by many customers at a departmental level to allow registration of systems. Customers would like a means to show which activation keys(s) were used to register a system so that they could track usage at a per-departmental level. 

Overall, there are several ways for customer to connect systems to the HCC and we should smartly handle as many of these cases as possible, including:
* Registered to Satellite via activation key (currently included in the satellite inventory upload plugin)
* Registered to hosted services via activation key
* Registered to hosted services via cloud-based auto-registration
* (Future) Registered to hosted services via team/workspace

h2. Additional Background
* In RHSM on the customer portal, we displayed the username of the user who registered the system if username/password was the authentication method. This was not good practice for data security, specifically for personally identifiable information (PII). We have no plans to expose this level of PII on the Hybrid Cloud Console and all requests specific to exposing username will be marked "Closed - Won't Do."
* Overall, we are moving away from username/password as an authentication method with activation keys, cloud-based auto-registration, and (soon) workspace registration being better patterns for our customers to adopt. We will focus our investments on those experiences.

h2. Request
As a user managing the inventory for my organization, I need better ways to organize and understand where systems came from, so that I can make process adjustments, create communication channels with groups who own systems, and have a better sense of how my user base is consuming RHEL.

Acceptance Criteria:
* For any given system, I can see how it came to be in the inventory.
* For any group of systems, I can search/filter/organize them by how they came to be in the inventory.

The Notifications of Insights does not yet support for Patch (Errata) notifications.
It would be a good way to modernize the Errata Notifications mailed to customers.

Background:
Currently customer is subscribed of the daily digest of the Errata Notifications on the regular RH Portal configured on the user profile. The daily digest is old fashioned mail concatenation based and has severe limitations from user perspective:
 - Only 20 errata per mail, with a new minor release with 200 errata it takes 10-30 (depending on also new errata) days to catch up
 - 60% of mail content is boiler plate repetition and not valuable content
 - Not sorted per RHEL minor release

If the (mail) notification is builds in RH Hybrid Cloud Console you have a green-field approach to build a modern and configurable errata notification process.
 - Modernize mails
 - More usable content in a single mail because it is not just contact of mails
 - Future Extension: Sorting of Errata per Product-Release
 - Future Extension: Configurable mails (e.g. interesting products)
 - Agile development process without impacting potential legacy customer business process on the mail format of the RH Portal mail

h2. Description of Problem

Red Hat Insights + Advisor can scan and inform about EOL packages well before they are EOL. 

The advisor includes ROL rules triggered when we detect approaching EOL or ELS of RH products\packages and Appstream modules. For EOL that happens at 30 days mark and for ELS it happens at 60 days mark. 

 

Once these rules are triggered :
 * They are displayed as advisor recommendations
 * They also trigger related events

 

But it's impossible to subscribe to EOL-only events to get notifications via email. One has to subscribe to all the Advisor Events to get weekly or monthly notifications via email and that does not include EOL-specific data.  
h2. How reproducible

(Always)
h2. Ask:
 * The advisor needs to have specific EOL-related events to be able to subscribe to.
 * The end users need to be able to configure Insights notifications to be sent 30 days prior to the end of life (EOL) of software packages.
 * The end user would prefer a more informative email from Insights Advisor that specifies which software/packages are reaching EOL in the next 30 days, along with any associated vulnerabilities, particularly the major ones. 
 *  [Optionally] It would be even better to allow the end-user to select how many days before, they want to receive the notification about EOL i.e. 30 days 60 days or 90 days

items.fromString:
h2. Feature Overview

Customers can launch their VMs and enroll/join them into an already existing Identity Management deployment. _This Feature is part of a collection of Features to enable support for various Identity Provider solutions._

When I provision my host(s), it can configure them to join an established {*}Identity Management in RHEL{*}* domain, so that users can authenticate to and access (subject to the domain's access policies) the host after launch.

{*}{{*}}Identity Management in RHEL\{*}: This is the branding of our product, we are not mentioning upstream solutions, but it refers to FreeIPA.
h2. Background, and strategic fit

Enterprise customers with established Identity Management deployments will want any new hosts they launch to become a part of their established domains. ImageBuilder and HMS launch services should provide this capability in an automated fashion. In other words, no additional user actions are required to enroll the machine post-launch.

This meets several customer goals:
 * Lower costs through increased automation
 * Improve security through access and security policies being applied to the machines immediately after launch.

We see it as an opportunity to bring small enterprise customers (or internal departments) which have their own *Identity Management in RHEL* domain, to provision hosts and take advantage of their own Identity Provider solution (mostly due to internal policies or compliance).

The implementation of this feature also delivers a framework for additional Identity Provider integrations in the future. (For example: Active Directory, Azure AD, AWS IAM, etc.)
h2. Glossary
 * {*}Blueprint{*}: A registered identity provider domain, making it available for use with the Domain Join feature.  The term is just a placeholder; the product might use a different name.

 * {*}Domain{*}: a deployment of an identity provider solution, such as Identity Management in RHEL.
 * {*}Domain Join{*}: enrolling a machine as a client of an identity management domain.
 * {*}Enrollment{*}: see *Domain Join*
 * {*}Host{*}: A VM, typically registered with the console.redhat.com Inventory and possibly created via the *Launch* workflow.
 * {*}Identity Management in RHEL{*}: Red Hat's identity provider solution.  The terms *IDM* and *FreeIPA* (the upstream project) are used interchangeably.
 * {*}Image{*}: A VM image available for use in the *Launch* workflow.  It was possibly created via {_}Image Builder{_}.
 * {*}Launch{*}: The Launch workflow, which creates VMs in the customer's clouds.
 * {*}Provisioning{*}: see *Launch*

h2. Delivery phases
 * *1: e2e* demo: The initial implementation of the backend service, registration UI, and enrollment workflow.  Assuming you are launching an image with the packages and configuration needed for the launched VM to join a registered domain.  The _Image Builder_ integration to actually build such an image is out of scope.
 * *2: IB* integration: Adding behaviour and UI to the Image Builder workflow so that users can easily build images that are capable of {_}Domain Join on Launch{_}.  Some integration with the _Launch_ service may also be required, and would be in scope for this phase.  This will also require solving the RPM delivery questions (how to get ipa-hcc onto customer images).
 * {*}3: Prod{*}uctionisation: Completion of operational requirements such as logging, metrics, ConsoleDot integration (search, appear in UI, etc).
 * {*}X{*}: Future phase(s): Requirements or enhancements to be addressed after initial delivery of the feature (MVP)

h2. Functional Requirements
|*Requirement*|*Notes*|*Phase*|
|Register *Identity Management in RHEL* domain in ConsoleDot, without storing any secrets or credentials in ConsoleDot.|This will be a separate workflow.  The result of registration is that the registered domain becomes available for Domain Join.|1|
|Being part of *Launch* workflow|Launched hosts shall (attempt to) join a registered Domain, assuming the image contains the required packages and configuration.|1|
|Being part of *Image Builder* workflow|Images can be general and intended for enrollment in arbitrary identity providers (or left unenrolled).  The choice ultimately happens at Launch.  Also, a Blueprint associated with an Image might have been deleted or disabled at Launch time.However it could still be useful to be able to _annotate_ an image with particular Blueprints as a _hint_ to the Launch workflow.|2|
|Heuristics for automatically selecting/suggesting a domain for image/provisioned machine.|To assist the user we can use data we know or can collect (e.g. via Insights) to suggest a Blueprint.|X|
|Identity Provider domain included in Launch "Blueprint"/"Template"|To be explored later on -> Automated way to grab domains from insights and provide that information to the end user
-------------------------------------
If IDM servers are already enrolled into inventory and we are aware of those servers/domains we can grab the settings and create/suggest that domain during the Domain Registration workflow.
We need to implement this capability in insights (to deliver the information about domains/servers into Insights), allowing us to proceed with the suggestion.
https://issues.redhat.com/browse/HMSIDM-160|2|
|Bulk Launch|Ability to launch more than one instance at a time using Domain Join feature|2|
|Removing machine from domain when it is removed/deleted|Discuss it further (See Non Functional Requirements)|X|
|Gracefully handle temporary IDM server unavailability.|IDM Server can be unavailable at launch/enroll time. We should ensure that the enrollment completes when the IDM server becomes available again.|X|
|Blueprint Validation during insertion (During "blueprint" (IdP) setup we can launch a VM, and attempt to join it, to verify the blueprint configuration.) *Non-Functional Requirement related (Availability)*|A way to validate if the blueprint/configuration added is correct and can be used - users can anticipate any kind of mistype or misconfiguration in advance, not only after launching the machine.
This does not guard against all join failure scenarios, e.g. image does not have required packages, image has conflicting crypto configuration, connectivity issue between cloud(s) in which VM launches and the IdP).|X|
|Create and manage Blueprint registrations, and selecting a Blueprint during Launch workflow|As for registrations, it is a privileged operation, and we will use ConsoleDot CIAM RBAC
As for Launch, I am not sure what the requirements should be ({*}Question{*})|2|
|Show machine join domain and status Inventory.|Example states: * No domain (customer does not want it joined to any domain)
 * Join requested, but not yet initiated
 * Join requested, initiated, but not yet completed
 * Join requested, initiated, and failed
 * Joined|X|
h2. Non-Functional Requirements

Please take a look at this nice guide talking about NFRs [Top 10 Architecture Characteristics / Non-Functional Requirements with Cheatsheet|https://blog.devgenius.io/top-10-architecture-characteristics-non-functional-requirements-with-cheatsheat-7ad14bbb0a9b]

 
|*Category*|*Requirement*|
|Scalability| - Create a set of configuration variables enabling setup of:
 - - How many hosts can be enrolled at the same time
 - - How many hosts are allowed per batch enrollment operation
 - - How much time do we wait between each batch operation
 - Majority of the settings being configurable can help us in the future.
 - Configurable by service operator (Red Hat), not the custome
Reason: [Amy] Running into a technical issue where around 96 client requests will stop the server from responding.  (listed as blocker from perf team notes) [IDM Performance Pipeline|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1374ZKPDf5btPqjwsXjje0SL77xTBGOaGyJiooK0f0gE/edit?usp=sharing] / [https://github.com/freeipa/freeipa-perftest/]
{*}Affinity{*}: “I would rather talk to you than talking to the other”  And the choice of which server is usually based on network proximity (geolocation). -> *Assumption that customer did the proper configuration, so it will resolve by itself.*
 
{*}Idea to Business{*}: Free Tier vs Premium Tier -> FYI [~accountid:70121:fbf6f091-363d-4cd8-a75e-49b39f643f6a] [~accountid:5fc4f1f20dd553006fb88ba1] [~accountid:70121:b0ab6618-4707-44c8-9350-b28bf813e8d6] 
Single host at a time vs batch
Limit the number of hosts can enroll (up to 50 hosts?)|
|Availability|{*}Assumption{*}:
 - Standard ConsoleDot SLOs for service availability apply.
 - For IDM server availability, customer assumes responsibility.

Customers can launch their VMs and enroll/join them into an already existing Identity Management deployment. _This Feature is part of a collection of Features to enable support for various Identity Provider solutions._

h2. Background, and strategic fit
